comparison: Both evaluate force field methodology (C94-C97) as SUPPORTED. OpenEval emphasizes methodological lineage and citations, while peer reviewers acknowledge this as a valuable starting point with validated prior work. Strong agreement on methodological foundation.

Both evaluate mechanistic interference claims (C68-C74, C86, C90) as UNCERTAIN. OpenEval notes these are speculative inferences requiring experimental validation with appropriate cautious language. Peer reviewers similarly emphasize these are 'putative' or 'conjectural' findings requiring experimental support. Strong agreement on uncertainty.

Both evaluate binding site identifications (C56-C67, C84-C89) as SUPPORTED. OpenEval emphasizes objective validation via PDB/PiSITE crystal structures. Peer reviewers find these 'interesting' and 'solid' but note they are computational predictions. Agreement on support with acknowledgment of computational nature.

Both evaluate electrostatic binding mechanism and correlations (C38-C43, C44-C45, C49-C50, C75-C76, C83) as SUPPORTED. OpenEval highlights linear correlations in Figure 2 and systematic optimization. Peer reviewers describe approach as 'well-tuned' with 'solid' evidence. Strong agreement on core findings.

Both evaluate background claims about C9orf72 and ALS/FTD (C1-C7, C16-C19, C36, C98-C100) as SUPPORTED. OpenEval notes appropriate citations to established literature. Peer reviewers accept this well-established context without challenge. Complete agreement on background.

Both evaluate NCT mechanism descriptions (C8-C15, C26-C35, C101) as SUPPORTED. OpenEval describes these as well-established mechanisms with appropriate citations. Peer reviewers accept this as necessary context without dispute. Complete agreement on established biological knowledge.

Both evaluate computational methodology and model construction (C20-C29, C37, C102-C104) as SUPPORTED. OpenEval validates 1BPA approach and justifies IBB domain exclusion. Peer reviewers explicitly praise the 'well-tuned' force field and note method 'goes beyond state of the art.' Strong agreement with peer enthusiasm.

Both evaluate length-dependent toxicity connection (C75-C77, C81, C91-C92) as UNCERTAIN/requiring validation. OpenEval notes correlation is plausible but causal link inferential. Peer reviewers emphasize this is an important hypothesis but requires experimental validation, describing it as 'putative' and 'a first step.' Agreement on need for experimental support.

Both evaluate differential binding patterns (C44-C48, C46-C48, C51-C54, C78, C82) as SUPPORTED. OpenEval emphasizes direct support from contact data in Figure 2a. Peer reviewers accept these patterns without challenge, describing evidence as 'solid' and 'well-reported.' Strong agreement.

Both evaluate salt-dependent binding claims (C49-C55) as SUPPORTED. OpenEval highlights Figure 2 data and electrostatic interpretation with polymer physics principles. Peer reviewers accept the electrostatic mechanism and correlations without challenge. Agreement on salt dependence findings.

Both evaluate RanGAP C-terminal binding context (C63-C64, C79-C80) as SUPPORTED. OpenEval cites structural studies for functional context. Peer reviewers do not challenge this finding, describing evidence as 'solid' with established literature support. Agreement on RanGAP findings.

Both evaluate RanGAP findings (C78-C81) as SUPPORTED with some inferential elements. OpenEval notes simulation data support with plausible but not definitive causal connection. Peer reviewers accept the binding evidence without challenge. Agreement on computational findings with acknowledged inferential aspects.

Both evaluate electrostatic model refinement (C82-C83) as SUPPORTED. OpenEval highlights improved R² values with dipole moment term. Peer reviewers accept this refinement as part of the 'well-tuned' computational approach. Agreement on model sophistication.

Both evaluate binding site summaries (C84-C90) as SUPPORTED for binding data but UNCERTAIN for functional interference (C90). OpenEval notes C90 requires experimental validation. Peer reviewers find binding sites 'interesting' but emphasize computational nature. Agreement with nuanced distinction between binding observation and functional inference.

Both evaluate main conclusions and future directions (C91-C93) as SUPPORTED for findings but speculative for therapeutic implications. OpenEval frames C92-C93 as reasonable speculation. Peer reviewers acknowledge as 'important starting point' and 'useful as first step.' Agreement on value with appropriate caveats.

Both evaluate simulation design and validation (C36-C37, C102-C104) as SUPPORTED. OpenEval emphasizes convergence demonstration and justified parameters. Peer reviewers praise methodology and note convergence in supplementary figures. Strong agreement on simulation quality.

Both evaluate arginine interaction chemistry (C98-C101) as SUPPORTED. OpenEval cites experimental work and established chemical knowledge. Peer reviewers accept this as necessary context for understanding cation-π interactions in the force field. Agreement on chemical basis.

Both evaluate experimental basis for protein selection (C16-C19) as SUPPORTED. OpenEval notes appropriate citations justify computational investigation. Peer reviewers accept this experimental foundation without challenge. Agreement on study rationale.

Both evaluate Ran's minimal binding (C67) as SUPPORTED. OpenEval notes consistency with low dipole moment and neutral charge. Peer reviewers accept this observation as consistent with the electrostatic mechanism. Agreement on this specific finding.
